title: ¿Qué hiciste?
goal: Tell what you did and where you went with the common irregular preterites.

lessons.title: I went, it was
lessons.notes:
**ser** and **ir** have the **same** preterite - one set of forms to learn for two verbs:
**yo** fui · **tú** fuiste · **él / ella / usted** fue · **nosotros** fuimos · **ellos / ustedes** fueron
Context tells them apart. With **a** + a place it's "went"; with a description it's "was":
**Fui a la playa.** = I went to the beach.
**Fue genial.** = It was great.
No accents on these: **fui**, **fue** are one syllable.

sentences.es: Ayer fui a la playa con Luis.
sentences.en: Yesterday I went to the beach with Luis.
accept_en: I went to the beach with Luis yesterday.

sentences.en: Where did you go on Saturday?
The party was great.

sentences.es: Fuimos a un concierto el viernes.
sentences.en: We went to a concert on Friday.

sentences.es: Mis padres fueron a México de vacaciones.
sentences.en: My parents went to Mexico on holiday.
accept_en: My parents went to Mexico on vacation.

sentences.en: The concert was very long.
How were the holidays?
It was a really nice day.
accept_en: It was a very nice day.
It was a very beautiful day.

lessons.title: What did you do?
lessons.notes:
**hacer** has its own stem in the preterite, **hic-**, and endings with no accents:
**yo** hice · **tú** hiciste · **él / ella / usted** hizo · **nosotros** hicimos · **ellos / ustedes** hicieron
Note **hizo** with a z (hico would sound like "hiko").
The big question: **¿Qué hiciste ayer?** = What did you do yesterday? To answer, use the verb for what you did, not hacer: **Fui al cine.**
Weather in the past uses hacer too: **Hizo calor.** = It was hot.
**No hice nada.** = I didn't do anything (Spanish happily doubles the negative).

items.note: Spain: la tarta. In Mexico una torta is a sandwich!

sentences.en: What did you do on the weekend?
accept_en: What did you do at the weekend?
What did you do over the weekend?

sentences.es: No hice nada, me quedé en casa.
sentences.en: I didn't do anything, I stayed at home.
accept_en: I did nothing, I stayed home.
I didn't do anything, I stayed home.

sentences.es: Hice una torta para la fiesta.
sentences.en: I made a cake for the party.
It was very hot yesterday.

sentences.es: Hicimos la tarea en la biblioteca.
sentences.en: We did the homework in the library.
accept_en: We did our homework in the library.
We did our homework at the library.

sentences.en: What did you all do last night?
accept_en: What did you do last night?
What did you guys do last night?

sentences.es: Mi hermano no hizo la cama.
sentences.en: My brother didn't make the bed.
accept_en: My brother didn't make his bed.

sentences.en: Last Saturday it was cold.

lessons.title: I had, I was
lessons.notes:
Several common verbs share a pattern: an irregular stem plus the endings **-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron**, with no accents.
**tener** -> **tuv-**: tuve · tuviste · tuvo · tuvimos · tuvieron
**estar** -> **estuv-**: estuve · estuviste · estuvo · estuvimos · estuvieron
**poder** -> **pud-**: pude · pudiste · pudo · pudimos · pudieron
Learn the **yo** form and the rest follows.
**estar** in the preterite tells how long or where for a finished stretch: **Estuve dos semanas en Chile.**
**no pude** means "I couldn't (and didn't)": **No pude ir.**

sentences.es: Ayer tuve un problema con el carro.
sentences.en: Yesterday I had a problem with the car.
accept_en: I had a problem with the car yesterday.
Yesterday I had trouble with the car.

sentences.en: My sister had a baby.
We were very lucky.
accept_en: We had a lot of luck.

sentences.en: I was in Chile for two weeks.
accept_en: I spent two weeks in Chile.
I stayed in Chile for two weeks.

sentences.en: Where were you all last night?
accept_en: Where were you guys last night?

sentences.en: Dinner was really delicious.

sentences.es: No pude ir a la fiesta.
sentences.en: I couldn't go to the party.
accept_en: I wasn't able to go to the party.

sentences.en: Were you able to talk to her?
accept_en: Did you manage to speak with her?
Did you get to talk to her?

sentences.en: What problem did you have?

lessons.title: Telling what happened
lessons.notes:
Three more irregulars you'll need to tell a story:
**venir** -> **vin-**: vine · viniste · vino · vinimos · vinieron
**decir** -> **dij-**: dije · dijiste · dijo · dijimos · **dijeron** (no i after j)
**ver** is regular but short, with no accents: vi · viste · vio · vimos · vieron
**pasar** means "to happen" (and "to spend" time): **¿Qué pasó?** = What happened?
When you report speech, **que** links it: **Me dijo que está cansado.** = He told me (that) he's tired. In English you can drop "that"; in Spanish **que** stays.

items.note: No accent when it links: dijo que... With an accent it asks: ¿qué?

sentences.en: What happened last night?

sentences.es: Carlos no vino a la fiesta.
sentences.en: Carlos didn't come to the party.
Why didn't you come yesterday?

sentences.es: Ella me dijo que está cansada.
sentences.en: She told me that she's tired.
accept_en: She told me she is tired.

sentences.en: I told him no.

sentences.es: Anoche vi una película muy buena.
sentences.en: Last night I saw a very good film.
accept_en: Last night I watched a really good movie.
I saw a very good film last night.
Last night I watched a very good movie.

sentences.es: Vimos a tu hermano en el parque.
sentences.en: We saw your brother in the park.
accept_en: We saw your brother at the park.

sentences.es: Pasamos el fin de semana en la playa.
sentences.en: We spent the weekend at the beach.
What did the teacher tell you?
accept_en: What did the teacher say to you?
